title: Any bot can qualify through the branch fallback
problem: The carve-out accepts every GitHub bot through `_is_bot_authored`. The task lookup can also fall back from the PR URL to the repository and head branch. A repo-native bot PR can therefore match a signal run by branch alone. The code then treats it as self-driving and bypasses the normal authorization gates. Generic `Bot` or `[bot]` status does not prove that the configured PostHog App created the PR.
suggestion: Require an exact PR binding for this authorization decision. Compare the event PR URL with the TaskRun's stored PR URL after the trusted backstop records it. If branch matching must remain, also verify the configured GitHub App author identity and an immutable run-to-branch association. Do not use generic bot status as proof of origin.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:144-215), the facade it calls (`find_signal_implementation_run`, products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:484-516), the lookup that facade delegates to (`find_task_run`, products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:29-98), branch seeding in products/signals/backend/auto_start.py:253, and the engine gates the flag relaxes (tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py:321-324, tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:590).
**Found:** the branch leg is unconditional. `find_task_run` tries `output__pr_url` first; when that returns nothing it falls through to `filter(branch=branch, task__repository__iexact=repository, state__wizard_head_branch__isnull=True).first()` (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:63-77). It does not require the run to lack a recorded PR URL, it does not exclude terminal runs (only the wizard leg at products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:90 does), and it applies no ordering. So one signals run keeps matching every same-name head branch in that repository forever, including after it already bound to a different PR.
**Found:** the `branch` column can hold the BASE branch, not a work branch. `auto_start.py:253` seeds the implementation run with `branch=base_branch`, and products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:34-35 records that "auto-start seeds it with the BASE branch and the agent server later overwrites it with the work branch". `find_task_run` already excludes wizard runs for exactly this false-match reason (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:64-66: "a same-repo PR whose head ref equals the base (e.g. 'main') would otherwise claim the run"). Signals runs get no equivalent exclusion.
**Found:** the same file already applies the guard this carve-out omits. products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:191-197 refuses to act on a branch match for a merge until `run_output.get("pr_url") == pr_url`, commented "requiring equality here keeps a same-branch webhook for a different PR from marking this run's PR as merged". The carve-out makes a larger decision on a weaker match.
**Found:** the facade test names the intended scope but the code does not enforce it — `test_branch_match_covers_runs_without_a_recorded_pr_url` (products/tasks/backend/tests/test_webhooks.py:1273). Stamphog's carve-out tests mock the facade wholesale (`_FIND_RUN`, products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:32), so no test drives the real branch fallback through the carve-out.
**Impact:** a repo-native bot PR that shares a head-branch name with any signals run in that repository passes `_is_bot_authored` (tasks.py:124-127) and the facade, so it receives the carve-out. The run then bypasses four gates — bot author, draft, `review_mode`, author write permission (tasks.py:872-880, tasks.py:944, tasks.py:967-969) — and stamps `inbox_review` provenance (tasks.py:1064). `review_local.py:321-324` converts that into `self_driving=True`, which drops the bot refusal and the draft prerequisite and adds a prompt block asserting self-driving provenance over untrusted PR content. An APPROVE verdict then posts a real GitHub approval on a PR the product's own invariant says must stay refused (products/stamphog/CLAUDE.md: "Identification is task linkage, never author-login matching").
**Impact:** caveat on today's reach — in this snapshot every production signals task sets `internal=True` (auto_start.py:261, report_generation/research.py:717, custom_agent/base.py:629) and the facade rejects internal tasks (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:508), so the carve-out looks inert here. That same condition would also disable review_hog's own inbox trigger (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:104), which contradicts this PR's stated behavior, so it reads as a stale-snapshot artifact rather than the intended state. It narrows current reachability; it does not repair the identification logic the PR ships.
**Priority:** lowered to should_fix. The trigger needs a head-branch name collision inside the same repository and team, plus an opted-in acting reviewer; fork heads are already excluded (tasks.py:173-178), so an outside attacker cannot reach it directly. The fix is small and precedented — reject the match when the run already records a different `pr_url` — and it restores exactly the scope the facade's own test claims.

title: The trusted prompt reports ready pull requests as drafts
problem: This block always states that the PR is a draft. A self-driving PR can become ready and receive a later commit. That commit triggers another review with `self_driving` still enabled. The trusted prompt then supplies false state, and no other prompt field shows the actual draft status.
suggestion: Make this text conditional on `pr.draft`. Pass the draft state into `_format_self_driving`, or use accurate text such as: `This review can run while the PR is a draft.`
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** every path that can set the engine flag — `tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py:321` reads `self_driving_review` from the hosted context, which `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451` sets from `run.output["inbox_review"]`, stamped by the webhook carve-out (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1064`) and the receiver leg (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1229`).
**Found:** neither stamping path requires draft state. `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:167-215`) gates on action in `{synchronize, reopened}` or a base retarget, bot authorship, repo-native head, config, task linkage, and the reviewer toggle — it never reads `pr["draft"]`. `process_inbox_pr_review` only checks `state == "open"` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1166`). A grep for `draft` across `temporal/`, `logic/`, `facade/`, and `tasks/` finds the state read only in `_review_skip_reason` (`tasks.py:226`), which the carve-out deliberately bypasses.
**Found:** so a self-driving PR that flips to ready and then receives a commit produces a run with `self_driving=True` and `pr.draft == False`, and `reviewer.py:698-700` still asserts "It is a draft on purpose".
**Found:** no other prompt field corrects it. With the flag set, `_check_prerequisites` (`tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:590`) skips the "PR is still in draft" issue, so the gate line reads "all clear" for draft and ready alike, and `pr.draft` appears nowhere else in the prompt — only in telemetry at `reviewer.py:363`.
**Impact:** the block the design treats as ground truth carries a false state fact for a ready-to-merge PR. The reviewer can grant draft-appropriate leniency to code that is about to merge, and can repeat the wrong claim in the posted verdict text, while a stamphog approval satisfies required reviews.
**Impact:** the fix is cheap and the data is already present — `_build_review_prompt` receives `pr` (`reviewer.py:449`) and `PRData.draft` is populated in both runtimes (`review_local.py:197`, `github.py:591`).

title: Fail-soft database check can flood error logs
problem: Every settings GET and PATCH calls the Stamphog database. During an outage, every request logs a full exception. The circuit breaker reduces connection time, but it still raises on each request. This can flood logs and error tracking during the outage.
suggestion: Rate-limit or sample this log. Prefer one log or metric for each circuit-breaker state change. Keep returning `False` so the endpoint remains available.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the call frequency of the settings endpoint from the frontend, the query the fail-soft block wraps, and the operator signal the circuit breaker already emits.
**Found:** the settings read is not polled. `loadSettings` runs once per scene mount (`products/review_hog/frontend/reviewHogSettingsLogic.ts:954-956` → `loadAll` at line 802 → the loader at line 446), plus once per user PATCH and once on `updateSettingsFailure` (line 811). The only interval poll in the logic re-loads `recentReviews` every 10s (`products/review_hog/frontend/reviewHogSettingsLogic.ts:758-762`), never the settings row. So the exception path fires at most a few times per user page visit, not per second.
**Found:** the scene that reaches this endpoint is alpha and flag-gated — `category: ProductItemCategory.UNRELEASED`, `flag: FEATURE_FLAGS.REVIEW_HOG` (`products/review_hog/manifest.tsx:28-32`). The reachable audience during an outage is small.
**Found:** `has_reviewable_repo_config` runs a single `exists()` query (`products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:120-125`), and the serializer holds one row per user, so there is no per-row amplification of either the query or the log.
**Found:** the per-state-change signal the suggestion asks for already exists one layer down. `posthog/db_circuit_breaker.py:248-254` emits `statsd.incr("product_db_circuit_breaker_opened")` and one `logger.warning` when the breaker opens, so an operator gets a bounded outage signal without any change to this serializer.
**Found:** `except Exception: logger.exception(...)` around a fail-soft read is the established idiom here — about 40 occurrences under `posthog/api/` alone. Adding a sampler or rate limiter only at this one call site would be an inconsistent local exception.
**Impact:** no user-visible defect and no realistic log flood. The endpoint stays available and returns `False`, which is the intended degradation. The proposed rate-limiting machinery guards a bounded, low-volume path that another layer already reports once per state change, so the finding falls under the criteria for overengineering and does not meet the bar.

title: The initial review handoff can be lost when the broker is unavailable
problem: This method publishes directly to Celery after the database transaction commits. The caller catches publication errors and only writes a log. A broker outage can therefore remove the only initial review request. No durable record exists for a later retry.
suggestion: Persist a pending review request before commit. Add a dispatcher that retries unpublished requests. Mark the request as dispatched only after Celery accepts it.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the only caller of `queue_inbox_pr_review` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:210-234), the receiver that drives it (`handle_task_run_saved`, receivers.py:72-139), the Celery task it dispatches (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109-1245), and every write path that touches `TaskRun.output` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2044+2074, api.py:2154, products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:292).
**Found:** the dispatch is not one-shot, so it is not "the only initial review request". The receiver fires on every `TaskRun` save whose `update_fields` include `output` (receivers.py:85-89), and receivers.py:76-79 states this is deliberate: "Repeat saves with an unchanged target re-fire it deliberately". The task's own docstring builds on that contract — products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1125-1128: "The receiver re-fires on every TaskRun output save carrying the PR URL, so dedupe keys on the PR's CURRENT head".
**Found:** such saves keep happening after the PR opens. `update_task_run` adds `output` to `update_fields` and saves on the agent-server PATCH surface (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2044, api.py:2074), `set_task_run_output` saves it too (api.py:2154), and receivers.py:5-7 records that a successful run "deliberately never leaves `in_progress`" because "the PR follow-up loop babysits the PR" — so further agent turns and output syncs are the normal path, not an exception.
**Found:** re-dispatch is safe by design, which is what makes the re-fire an actual recovery rather than a duplicate-review hazard. `process_inbox_pr_review` dedupes on the PR's current head under a row lock and restarts a stranded `QUEUED` run instead of stacking a second one (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1202-1221).
**Found:** a second independent path also covers the PR. Later `synchronize` / `reopen` / base-retarget deliveries re-review through the webhook carve-out (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1119), so any push after the outage produces a review.
**Found:** the swallow the finding points at is a deliberate, correct choice, not an oversight. receivers.py:213-214 documents it — "the broker being down must never surface into the saver" — and the module docstring at receivers.py:80 notes the body "executes inside tasks' save path and must never raise into it". Letting a broker error propagate would break `TaskRun` persistence for the agent run itself, which is strictly worse than a missed review.
**Impact:** this does not meet the bar. The residual exposure needs a broker outage that straddles the last `output` save that run will ever make, with no later push to the PR — and while the broker is down, a persisted pending row could not be dispatched either. The worst outcome is that one draft PR gets no Stamphog review, which is the behavior before this PR; no approval is left standing over unreviewed code (the stale-approval retraction paths are untouched), and nothing is lost or corrupted.
**Impact:** the suggested remedy is the overengineering shape the criteria drop — a new pending-request table, a dispatcher, and dispatched-state bookkeeping to harden one fire-and-forget facade call, against a failure mode two existing paths already self-heal. It also cuts against the repo convention of `transaction.on_commit` + `.delay()` for Celery dispatch.

title: A worker crash can discard the initial review task
problem: Celery acknowledges this task before execution because acks_late is not enabled. A worker crash after acknowledgement loses the task. This path has no webhook redelivery, so the initial review can remain missing. The existing head-based deduplication already makes task redelivery safe.
suggestion: Set acks_late=True and reject_on_worker_lost=True on process_inbox_pr_review. Keep the current deduplication so a replacement worker can process a redelivered task safely.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the decorator on `process_inbox_pr_review` against its siblings in the same module, the global Celery configuration (`posthog/settings/*.py`, `posthog/celery.py`), the webhook entry point that feeds the comparison path (products/stamphog/backend/presentation/webhooks.py:35-64), and the recovery mechanism the task documents and implements.
**Found:** the premise that distinguishes this path is wrong. The reviewer argues this task deserves `acks_late` because, unlike the webhook path, it "has no webhook redelivery". The webhook view returns `HttpResponse(status=202)` immediately after `.delay()` (products/stamphog/backend/presentation/webhooks.py:63-64), so GitHub's delivery is acknowledged at the HTTP layer and GitHub never redelivers based on task outcome. A worker killed after Celery ack loses `process_pull_request_event` exactly as it would lose this task. The two paths have identical worker-loss exposure, so this flags the module-wide default rather than anything the PR introduces.
**Found:** the in-code phrase the finding echoes means something else. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1155-1156 says "no webhook redelivery behind it" to justify explicit `.retry()` on transient in-task failures, which the author does at tasks.py:1150, 1162, 1165, and 1237. It is not a claim about a crash after acknowledgement.
**Found:** a designed, documented recovery already covers a lost dispatch. tasks.py:1124-1128 states the receiver "re-fires on every TaskRun output save carrying the PR URL", and the head-keyed dedupe under `select_for_update` (tasks.py:1198-1221) makes each refire either a no-op or a restart of a stranded `QUEUED` run. products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:76-79 confirms repeat firing is deliberate, and receivers.py:85-89 shows every `output`-touching save reaches the receiver — saves that keep occurring after the PR opens (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2044+2074, api.py:2154). Later pushes are covered separately by the webhook carve-out (tasks.py:1119).
**Found:** the code matches both the local and repo-wide convention. `process_installation_event` (tasks.py:721) and `process_pull_request_event` (tasks.py:809) carry the identical `@shared_task(ignore_result=True, max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=5)`, and there is no global `task_acks_late` — only a handful of deliberate per-task opt-ins (posthog/tasks/exporter.py:48, posthog/tasks/tasks.py:348, posthog/tasks/usage_report.py:113, products/visual_review/backend/tasks/tasks.py:41).
**Impact:** this does not meet the bar. The trigger needs a hard worker kill (OOM, node loss) inside the short window between ack and completion — Celery's warm shutdown drains in-flight tasks on an ordinary deploy — and even then the next `TaskRun` output save or the next push re-triggers the review. The worst outcome is that one draft PR misses its draft-time review, which is the behavior before this PR; nothing is corrupted and no approval is left standing over unreviewed code.

title: A resolver failure can leave a stale approval active
problem: A synchronize event calls the inbox resolver before it dismisses the old approval. If the task lookup or toggle resolver raises, the task retries at line 879. It never reaches the dismissal at lines 887-898. After the retry limit, the old approval can still satisfy branch protection for unreviewed commits.
suggestion: Dismiss stale approvals before the inbox lookup for every head-changing event. The task can then retry the lookup and review without leaving the old approval active. Use a neutral dismissal message because the task does not yet know whether a new review will run.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the ordering at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:870-903, what `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` can raise (tasks.py:179-205), the retraction helper's own cost and preconditions (`_retract_stale_approvals_on_skip`, tasks.py:483-516 → `dismiss_stale_approvals_for_head`, products/stamphog/backend/logic/approvals.py:24-66), the resolver it calls across the product boundary (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:144-207 → products/signals/backend/report_generation/resolve_reviewers.py:304-332), and whether any other path recovers the missed dismissal.
**Found:** the retry does not fall through to the dismissal. tasks.py:879 raises `process_pull_request_event.retry(exc=e)` from inside the `except` block, so the whole task restarts from the top; once `max_retries=3` is spent (tasks.py:809), `retry()` raises `MaxRetriesExceededError` and the task dies before ever reaching tasks.py:887-898.
**Found:** nothing else retracts afterwards. The webhook view already returned `HttpResponse(status=202)` right after `.delay()` (products/stamphog/backend/presentation/webhooks.py:63-64), so GitHub never redelivers. No `ReviewRun` starts on this path, so the workflow's `dismiss_stale_approvals` and the terminal own-approvals sweep never run. The retraction returns only if another head-changing delivery arrives later, and `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS` is only `{synchronize, reopened}` (tasks.py:49) — if the PR receives no further push, the approval stands indefinitely.
**Found:** the change couples a safety action to subsystems it does not need. The retraction needs only the stamphog product DB (`PullRequest`/`ReviewRun`, tasks.py:501-509, approvals.py:44-53) plus GitHub. The new pre-step additionally reads the tasks DB via `find_signal_implementation_run` (tasks.py:191) and the main DB via the review_hog resolver (`SignalReportArtefact`, `Team`, `User`, `OrganizationMembership`, `UserSocialAuth`, `Integration` — receivers.py:180-202, resolve_reviewers.py:314-332). A partial incident in those, or a deterministic defect in the cross-product resolver, blocks a dismissal that has no dependency on either.
**Found:** the resolver is called bare. tasks.py:205 invokes `resolver(...)` with no local guard. review_hog wraps its own receiver body in `except Exception` because it must never raise into the tasks save path (receivers.py:140-141), but that protection does not extend to this call site. The carve-out was hardened for "review_hog isn't installed" (tasks.py:202-204, fail-closed) and not for "the resolver raises".
**Found:** the suggested reorder is cheap and matches the product's own stated pattern. `_retract_stale_approvals_on_skip` early-returns after one DB read when no `PullRequest` row exists (tasks.py:507-508), and `dismiss_stale_approvals_for_head` touches GitHub only when a standing approval sits at a different head (approvals.py:54-55) — so running it first adds no GitHub traffic for ordinary bot PRs. products/stamphog/CLAUDE.md states the workflow "runs `dismiss_stale_approvals` FIRST" precisely as a fail-closed measure, "if any later step crashes, the prior approval is already gone"; this path inverts that order. The only real cost is the message choice, since `_INBOX_OPT_OUT_DISMISS_MESSAGE` vs `_UNTRUSTED_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE` (tasks.py:897) needs the carve-out result.
**Impact:** on a `synchronize` of a self-driving inbox PR that already carries a stamphog approval, a sustained or deterministic failure in the carve-out lookup leaves that approval standing over the new, unreviewed commits — a direct breach of the product's headline invariant ("No stamphog approval may remain standing over commits it didn't review"). Base-retarget deliveries are safe, because tasks.py:853-863 retracts before any of this; only `synchronize` and `reopened` are exposed.
**Priority:** lowered to should_fix. A transient blip self-corrects, because the retry re-runs the whole task and the successful attempt performs the retraction, delayed by roughly 15 seconds. Losing the retraction outright needs the failure to persist across all four attempts or to be deterministic, so this is not reachable on a healthy path — but there is no recovery once it happens, and the fix is a small reorder.

title: The toggle gate does not match the promised assignee behavior
problem: This contract says one acting reviewer controls the review. The PR intent says any assigned reviewer can opt in. The resolver selects one user. An opted-in secondary assignee cannot enable Stamphog when the selected reviewer opted out.
suggestion: Resolve all assigned reviewers and select one who enabled `stamphog_review_inbox_prs`. Store that user's ID as the acting reviewer. Update README line 14 and add a test where the primary reviewer opted out and a secondary reviewer opted in.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** The acting-reviewer resolution and both toggle call sites in `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py`, the flagged `products/stamphog/AGENTS.md` lines 85-87, `products/stamphog/README.md` line 14, the serializer `help_text` and the switch copy in `CodeReviewScene.tsx`, the migration order of the two toggles, and `products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py`.
**Found:** `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` returns exactly one user id — `created_by` when that user is in the assigned set, else `resolved[0]` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:206). Both gates read that one user's toggle: the receiver leg at products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126 and the webhook-leg resolver at products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:154.
**Found:** The flagged documentation states this same contract, so there is no doc/code contradiction to fix. AGENTS.md line 86 says "whose acting reviewer opted in", and README line 14 says "gated by the acting reviewer's per-user `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle". The "at least one of the assigned users" wording appears only in the pull request description prose, which is not a code or documentation contract.
**Found:** The single-acting-reviewer rule is a settled decision, not a new choice in this change. Its docstring records dated maintainer decisions (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:167-169), and it already gates the pre-existing `review_inbox_prs` leg, which shipped in migration `0008_reviewusersettings.py`. Only `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` is new (migration `0019_...`), and it reuses that resolution on purpose so the two legs stay symmetric.
**Impact:** The one named consequence — a secondary opted-in assignee gets no Stamphog run when the acting reviewer opted out — fails closed. No review runs and no approval lands on unchecked code. The suggestion asks for a behavior change to shared, pre-existing resolution logic (plus a README edit and a new test) on the strength of a sentence in the pull request body. That is a design preference, not a correctness, security, or contract defect, so it does not meet the bar.

title: The initial task trusts caller-supplied PR provenance
problem: The task accepts `pr_url`, `task_run_id`, `signal_report_id`, and `acting_user_id` as trusted facts. It does not load the TaskRun or confirm that the run produced this PR. The run output is writable through the `task:write` API. A caller can set it to another open PR in a configured repository. The task then marks that PR as self-driving. This mark bypasses the bot, draft, review-mode, and author-permission gates. The workflow can post a real approval on an unrelated PR.
suggestion: Load `task_run_id` within `team_id` before fetching the PR. Confirm its task is non-internal and has the supplied signal report. Confirm the task repository and stored PR URL match the fetched PR. Also require a repository-native head and the expected machine author. Derive all provenance fields from these records instead of trusting the Celery arguments.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the full argument path — the writer that can set `output.pr_url` (`set_output`, products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1101-1109; `update_task_run`, products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2038-2044), the attested-key policy (`_apply_caller_output`, facade/api.py:1770-1788), the receiver that forwards the URL (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:92-139), the facade pass-through (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:149-155), the task body (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1130-1234), and where the provenance lands in the engine (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451, tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py:321-324, tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:590).
**Found:** `pr_url` is caller-writable by design. `_WEBHOOK_ATTESTED_RUN_OUTPUT_KEYS` is only `{"pr_merged"}` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:1770), and `_apply_caller_output` explicitly anticipates the caller repointing the run: "when the caller points the run at a different `pr_url` the stored flag described the old PR and is dropped" (facade/api.py:1778-1780). The `set_output` endpoint documents the field as "e.g., PR URL, commit SHA" and requires only `task:write` (presentation/views/api.py:1099-1105).
**Found:** the principal holding that scope is the sandboxed implementation agent. `auto_start.py:257` grants `posthog_mcp_scopes="full"` so the agent can write task artefacts, and that agent runs an LLM over repository content. products/stamphog/CLAUDE.md treats exactly this combination as dangerous for its own sandbox: "Never switch to `include_internal_scopes=True` — that drags `task:write` into a sandbox running an LLM over untrusted PR content."
**Found:** nothing between the write and the review re-checks the PR. The receiver validates the *task* (`signal_report_id` present, not `internal` — receivers.py:98-105) but forwards `pr_url` unvalidated (receivers.py:93, 130-139); `queue_inbox_pr_review` is a bare `.delay()` (facade/api.py:149-155); and `process_inbox_pr_review` never loads the `TaskRun`. It derives the repository from the attacker-supplied URL (tasks.py:1130-1134), accepts *any* synced+enabled config for that repository in the team rather than the task's repository (tasks.py:1140-1147), and requires only `state == "open"` plus a head sha (tasks.py:1166-1174) before stamping `inbox_review` from the Celery arguments (tasks.py:1176-1181, 1223-1230).
**Found:** the checks the webhook leg performs are all absent here. That leg verifies bot authorship (tasks.py:169), a repo-native head to exclude forks (tasks.py:173-178), task linkage via `find_signal_implementation_run` (tasks.py:191), and re-checks team scope (tasks.py:199). The receiver leg has none of them, and it also has no `_review_mode_skip_reason` and no `_author_lacks_write_permission` equivalent — the gate tasks.py:960-962 keeps specifically so a blip cannot "mint approvals for under-privileged authors".
**Found:** the provenance is trusted downstream with no re-derivation. activities.py:448-451 sets `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))` and comments that it is stamped "only after positively linking the PR to a signals implementation run"; products/stamphog/CLAUDE.md repeats that both trigger paths are linkage-verified. `_start_review_workflow` (tasks.py:366-380) adds no validation. So the documented invariant holds for the webhook leg only.
**Impact:** a holder of `task:write` on one team can point a live signals run's `output.pr_url` at any open PR in any of that team's stamphog-configured repositories and have Stamphog review it as trusted self-driving work: the bot-author refusal and draft prerequisite are dropped (review_local.py:324, review_pr.py:590), the repo's `review_mode` opt-in and the author-write-permission gate are never consulted on this leg, fork heads are not excluded, the prompt is given a TRUSTED provenance block (tools/pr-approval-agent/reviewer.py:683-692), and an APPROVE verdict posts a real GitHub approval that satisfies required reviews.
**Impact:** the same gap is reachable without an adversary. Any wrong `pr_url` recorded on the run — including one written by the tasks webhook backstop's branch-keyed match (`_record_run_pr_url`, products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:184-185) — is reviewed as self-driving with no verification, so this is a correctness defect as well as an authorization one.

title: The worker does not recheck the review opt-in
problem: The receiver checks the user toggle before it publishes the Celery task. The worker later trusts the supplied `acting_user_id`. A delayed or retried task can approve a PR after the user disables the toggle or loses the assignment. This creates a time-of-check to time-of-use gap in the approval gate.
suggestion: Resolve the current acting reviewer inside `process_inbox_pr_review`. Use the registered resolver after the task and signal report validation. Stop when no current reviewer has `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` enabled. Store the newly resolved user ID in the provenance.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the toggle read and dispatch in products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:114-139, the delay between dispatch and execution (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:149-155, products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109 and its retry countdowns at tasks.py:1150/1162/1165/1237), every consumer of `acting_user_id` in stamphog, and the remediation path for an approval left standing after an opt-out.
**Found:** the window is not a wait — it is scheduling latency. `_start_stamphog_review` runs in `transaction.on_commit` and calls `.delay()` with no countdown (receivers.py:131-139, facade/api.py:149-155), so the worker normally picks the task up within the same second the toggle was read. The only widening is the rate-limit retry at tasks.py:1162 (`countdown=max(e.retry_after or 0, 60)`), which needs GitHub to throttle the PR fetch and the user to flip the setting inside that window.
**Found:** a stale `acting_user_id` has no behavioral consequence. Grepping every use in products/stamphog shows it is only carried into provenance (tasks.py:1180, tasks.py:213) and never read back. The engine flag is `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))` — presence only, not identity (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451) — and the sandbox credential is minted under `repo_config.connected_by_user_id`, not the acting reviewer (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:123). So the "loses the assignment" half of the claim affects attribution in analytics and the UI, nothing more.
**Found:** an approval that lands just after an opt-out is already remediated by design, not left standing. The next head-changing delivery resolves `opted_out` and dismisses through `_INBOX_OPT_OUT_DISMISS_MESSAGE` (tasks.py:894-898, tasks.py:904-909), which is the documented rule in products/stamphog/CLAUDE.md that "dismissal is never preference-gated".
**Found:** the webhook leg's resolver re-check (tasks.py:201-207) is not a missing counterpart here. That leg fires on a push that can arrive days after the original opt-in, so re-reading the toggle answers a genuinely different question. The receiver leg reads the same `ReviewUserSettings` row moments earlier in the same save flow (receivers.py:114-126).
**Impact:** this does not meet the bar. The worst realistic outcome is one unwanted automated review, and possibly one approval, on the user's own team's self-driving draft PR, inside a sub-second window, undone by the opt-out dismissal on the next push. No authorization boundary is crossed — the toggle is a team member's own preference, and it was checked.
**Impact:** the proposed remedy also has a cost that argues against it as a standalone change: it moves the cross-product resolver (`SignalReportArtefact` plus org-member resolution, receivers.py:180-202) onto the initial-review path, adding a failure surface to a task whose exception handling already retries against several databases.

title: The carve-out trusts an unvalidated boolean
problem: This code converts every truthy JSON value into authority to bypass the bot and draft gates. The initial inbox path accepts a task-provided PR URL. It does not verify the fetched PR's bot author or native head repository before it stamps this field. A value such as "false" also becomes true. The engine can therefore approve a human or fork PR under the self-driving exception.
suggestion: Fail closed at this boundary. Require `context.get("self_driving_review") is True`. Enable the exception only when `author_is_bot` is true and the raw head repository matches `context["repo"]`. The server must also link the task identifiers to that exact PR before it creates the run. Keep the normal gates when any check fails. Add negative tests for a human draft, a fork PR, and string values such as `"false"`.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** both legs that stamp the provenance the engine flag is derived from, plus every producer of the `pr_url` they act on.
**Found:** the webhook leg verifies the two facts the carve-out depends on — `_is_bot_authored(pr)` and `head.repo.full_name == repository` — with an explicit fork-safety comment (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169-178`). The initial leg verifies neither: `process_inbox_pr_review` parses the URL, resolves a config for that repository, fetches the PR, and checks only `state == "open"` and a non-empty head sha before writing `output={"inbox_review": ...}` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1130-1181`). The facade in between validates nothing (`products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128-155`).
**Found:** that leg also never runs the two gates the webhook path only bypasses for identified inbox PRs — `_review_mode_skip_reason` (`tasks.py:944`) and `_author_lacks_write_permission` (`tasks.py:968`). So a PR reviewed through this leg passes no review-mode, author-association, or push-access check at all.
**Found:** the URL is whatever sits in `TaskRun.output["pr_url"]` (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:93,126-139`). One producer is fork-safe: the GitHub webhook backstop writes it only when `head.repo.full_name` equals the installed repo (`products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:178-185`). The other is not: `set_output` accepts any `pr_url` string under the `task:write` scope, and `validate_set_output` only applies a task's optional `json_schema` (`products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1107`, `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2123-2136,2139-2154`) — no check that the PR is in the task's repository, repo-native, or bot-authored.
**Found:** nothing downstream recovers the missing checks. `fetch_review_context` holds the full PR object yet only reads `inbox_review` to suppress the familiarity fetch (`products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:237`), and `activities.py:451` turns the same stored value straight into the engine flag. The engine's remaining gates are prerequisites, deny-list, size, and tier — none looks at the head repository or the author.
**Impact:** a self-driving carve-out review, whose APPROVE posts a real GitHub approval that satisfies required reviews, can be granted to a PR that is neither bot-authored nor repo-native, including an external fork PR. The reviewer prompt also asserts verified inbox provenance for it (`tools/pr-approval-agent/reviewer.py:694-702`). Both checks are cheap and the data is already fetched, so mirroring the webhook leg closes it.
**Impact:** the `bool()` half of the finding is not the defect. The only producer is `bool(output.get("inbox_review"))` (`activities.py:451`) serialized by `build_reviewer_invocation` (`products/stamphog/backend/logic/reviewer.py:131`), so a JSON string such as `"false"` has no path into the context; `is True` there is hardening only.

title: Inbox provenance is granted without verifying the pull request
problem: The receiver trusts output.pr_url after checking only the task type and user toggle. The queued task does not bind this URL to task_run_id or task.repository. It also does not verify the fetched PR author or its head repository. An unrelated PR can receive inbox provenance and bypass Stamphog's normal review gates.
suggestion: Before creating the review, load task_run_id through the tasks facade. Match the team, signal report, repository, PR URL, and head branch. Verify that the PR is bot-authored and has a repository-native head. Reject every mismatch. Add tests for human PRs, forks, different task repositories, and mismatched runs.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the receiver's PR leg (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:106-139`, `210-231`), the queued task it hands off to (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110-1234`), the sibling webhook leg's carve-out (`tasks.py:144-215`), the tasks facade binding (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:484-516`), the `output.pr_url` write paths, and the existing tests on both legs.
**Found:** the receiver reads `task.repository` at `receivers.py:106` but uses it only for the branch leg (`receivers.py:119`). The PR leg at `receivers.py:130-138` forwards `pr_url` untouched, so the PR's repository is never compared with the task's repository.
**Found:** the queued task verifies only four things: a parseable URL, a synced+enabled repo config for that URL's repository on this team (`tasks.py:1140-1147`), an open PR (`tasks.py:1166`), and a non-empty head sha (`tasks.py:1170`). It receives `task_run_id` but never loads that run — it only copies the id into provenance (`tasks.py:1176-1181`) and stamps it on the new run (`tasks.py:1229`). No bot-author check, no head-repository check, no PR-to-run binding.
**Found:** the sibling webhook leg performs every one of those missing checks: `_is_bot_authored(pr)` at `tasks.py:169`, a head-repository equality guard at `tasks.py:176-178` whose comment states "on a fork PR head.ref is attacker-controlled ... a branch-keyed task match could bind an unrelated fork PR to a run", and `find_signal_implementation_run(team_id=..., repository=repo, pr_url=..., head_branch=...)` at `tasks.py:191-200`, which binds the PR to a non-internal signal-report run in the config's team. Its docstring calls this "positive identification only". The receiver leg's own docstring instead asserts the property it never verifies: "the PR is a bot-authored draft by construction — the webhook path pre-filters both" (`tasks.py:1116-1119`). Those pre-filters do not run on this leg.
**Found:** the stamped provenance is exactly what disarms the protective gates. `ReviewRun.output["inbox_review"]` sets `self_driving_review` for the engine (`products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451` → `products/stamphog/backend/logic/reviewer.py:101-131`), which relaxes the bot-author refusal and the draft prerequisite and replaces human-author trust context with a trusted provenance block. It also suppresses the author trust lookup (`activities.py:237-238`), and on later deliveries it bypasses the review-mode gate (`tasks.py:944`) and the author write-permission gate (`tasks.py:968`). This leg is the one that posts the first real GitHub approval.
**Found:** a wrong `pr_url` does not need an attacker. `find_task_run`'s branch leg matches on head ref plus repository only (`products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:64-76`), so a repo-native PR whose head branch collides with a signals run's branch gets its URL written into that run (`webhooks.py:184-185`); the fork case is guarded there, the same-repository collision is not. `output.pr_url` is also directly caller-writable — `_apply_caller_output` at `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:1773-1788` exists precisely because "the caller points the run at a different `pr_url`" is a modeled case.
**Found:** the test suite mirrors the gap. The webhook leg has `test_inbox_carve_out_requires_task_linkage` (`products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:875`). The receiver-leg tests have no equivalent: `_inbox_pr()` (`test_tasks.py:909`) sets neither an author nor a head repository, and nothing asserts that a human-authored or fork PR is rejected on this path.
**Impact:** confirmed gate bypass. Within a team that has Stamphog synced on a repository and one opted-in reviewer, any open PR in that repository can be given inbox provenance by pointing a signals run's `output.pr_url` at it. Stamphog then reviews it with the bot-author refusal, draft prerequisite, review-mode gate, and author write-permission gate all disabled, and can post a real GitHub approval on a human or outside-contributor PR. Tenant isolation holds (`for_team` plus the per-team repo config), which bounds the blast radius to repositories the team already connected, but the carve-out itself stops being narrow — the exact property this product documents as its core invariant.

title: The Stamphog gate ignores later opted-in assignees
problem: _resolve_assigned_reviewer returns only the assigned task creator or the first resolved reviewer. Both Stamphog paths check only that user's toggle. No review runs when the first reviewer opted out but another assigned reviewer opted in. This conflicts with the requirement that any opted-in assignee can enable the review.
suggestion: Keep the canonical resolver for ReviewHog. Add a Stamphog resolver that checks all resolved assignees. Prefer the assigned task creator when opted in. Otherwise, select the first opted-in assignee. Use this resolver for both initial reviews and webhook re-reviews. Add multi-assignee tests for both paths.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the resolver and both its callers (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:111-156`, `159-207`), the toggle field definitions (`products/review_hog/backend/models.py:275-294`), the reviewer-artefact cardinality (`products/signals/backend/report_generation/resolve_reviewers.py:30`, `182`), and the existing receiver tests (`products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py`).
**Found:** the described behavior is pinned by a dedicated pre-existing test. `test_opted_out_canonical_reviewer_blocks_the_review` (`test_inbox_trigger.py:228-238`) builds the exact scenario — bob is canonical and not opted in, alice is a later assignee and opted in — and asserts `mock_start.assert_not_called()`. Its comment states the rule: "The canonical assignee's toggle is THE gate for background-created runs: if they kept the default off, a later reviewer's opt-in must not hijack whose options the review runs with." A second test reinforces it (`test_inbox_trigger.py:254-267`): "no review runs even though the creator did".
**Found:** the rule carries an explicit maintainer attribution in the resolver docstring — "Otherwise the **first** resolved reviewer is canonical (maintainer decisions, 2026-07-02/03)" (`receivers.py:167-168`) — and a further test pins the ordering itself (`test_inbox_trigger.py:205-226`, "maintainer decision").
**Found:** this PR does not introduce the semantics; it reuses them. `review_inbox_prs` and `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` both default to `False` (`models.py:293-294`), so the pre-existing ReviewHog toggle already behaves identically for a non-canonical assignee. The module docstring states the reuse deliberately: "The same resolved acting reviewer carries a second, independent toggle" (`receivers.py:17`). The new resolver differs from the old path only in which toggle it reads, which is what `test_resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer_keys_on_the_stamphog_toggle` (`test_inbox_trigger.py:371-387`) verifies.
**Found:** the "requirement that any opted-in assignee can enable the review" does not exist in the codebase. It appears only in the pull request description's prose. Every in-code statement of intent — the resolver docstring, the module docstring, and two negative tests — states the opposite rule.
**Found:** the single-reviewer rule also serves a purpose beyond gating. The acting reviewer supplies the perspectives, blind spots, validator, and urgency threshold that drive the ReviewHog review (`receivers.py:169-172`), and per-user configs cannot be merged. Keeping one definition of "acting reviewer" for both toggles gives the receiver leg and the webhook re-review resolver the same answer for a run.
**Impact:** does not meet the bar. The behavior is the documented, tested, maintainer-decided design, so the premise that it conflicts with a requirement is mistaken. It also fails closed — the outcome is a review that does not start, never an unwanted review or approval. The suggestion would split reviewer resolution between the two products and between the two legs, which is a product decision the maintainer already settled the other way, not a defect fix. The residual wart (a non-canonical user's toggle silently does nothing, with no explanation in the UI) applies equally to the pre-existing toggle and belongs in copy or docs, not as a blocking logic finding on this PR.

title: Post-filtering an unscoped run can hide a valid match
problem: `find_task_run` selects one run before this facade applies the team and self-driving checks. Multiple teams or runs can reference the same PR or branch. An unrelated run can win the query, after which this facade returns `None` without checking the valid run.
suggestion: Apply `team_id`, `task__internal=False`, and `task__signal_report_id__isnull=False` inside the lookup query. Add deterministic ordering for the branch lookup and prefer active runs as the PR URL lookup does.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** both legs of the delegated lookup (`find_task_run`, products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:36-98), every writer of `output.pr_url` (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:212, products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2043, api.py:2154), whether successor runs inherit a predecessor's `output.pr_url`, and what `branch` actually holds on the internal signal-report tasks that could win the branch leg (products/signals/backend/report_generation/research.py:710 with `internal=True` at research.py:717, products/signals/backend/auto_start.py:253).
**Found:** on the `pr_url` leg the duplicate set cannot produce a hidden valid match. The leg is already repository-scoped when a repository is supplied (webhooks.py:42-43), and the facade always supplies it (facade/api.py:504). The documented duplicate case is "a terminal original and its live resume" of the same task (webhooks.py:37-40), and I found no path that copies `output.pr_url` onto a different task's run — the field is written per-run by the agent server or by the webhook backstop onto the run it matched. Runs of the same task share `task.signal_report_id` and `task.internal`, so every candidate yields the identical post-filter outcome.
**Found:** on the branch leg, the runs that could win over a valid one carry a *base* branch value, so the collision only exists in the case where `None` is the correct answer. `auto_start.py:253` and `research.py:710` seed `branch` with the checkout branch, and products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:34-35 records that the field "seeds it with the BASE branch". A head ref equal to a base branch is exactly the false-positive shape; suppressing the match there is the desired behavior, not a lost match. Distinct tasks in one team otherwise get distinct work branches, so there is no ordinary duplicate.
**Found:** the remaining route needs the same GitHub repository connected to two PostHog teams *plus* a locator collision between them, and it chains through the branch-fallback weakness that is already reported separately. That is a compound speculation, not a trigger real inputs hit.
**Impact:** the failure direction is fail-closed. When the post-filter rejects the winner, the facade returns `None` and the carve-out simply does not fire — the PR keeps today's bot-author skip. No wrong approval, no cross-tenant leak (the team check still runs, it just returns nothing), no data loss. The worst outcome is a silently missing self-driving review, which is the behavior before this PR.
**Impact:** the non-determinism the suggestion raises (the branch leg calls `.first()` with no `order_by`, webhooks.py:67-75) is real, but on its own it only makes the *false-positive* branch match arbitrary rather than hiding a valid one — the substance there belongs to the finding that flags the branch fallback itself, not here. Pushing `team_id`, `internal`, and `signal_report_id` into the query would also mean changing `find_task_run`, which the GitHub webhook backstop shares (webhooks.py:159), so it is a refactor of a shared lookup rather than a local fix, weighed against no demonstrated wrong behavior.

title: Initial Stamphog dispatch can be lost permanently
problem: The receiver does not persist the Stamphog dispatch. `_start_stamphog_review` catches broker errors and returns. No later process retries the initial dispatch. Bot draft webhooks do not start this review, so a short broker outage can skip it permanently.
suggestion: Persist an idempotent dispatch record before commit. Publish it after commit, and use a scheduled worker to retry pending records. Use the task run and PR URL as the deduplication key.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the dispatch path (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126-139`, `210-234`), the receiver's re-entry conditions (`receivers.py:72-96`), the queued task's refire handling (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110-1234`), the webhook carve-out's action scope (`tasks.py:49`, `167`), the run-output write path, and the test that pins this contract.
**Found:** the claim that no later process retries is not accurate — two automatic re-entry paths exist. First, the receiver re-fires on any later save that touches `output`: it only skips when `update_fields` is supplied and omits `output` (`receivers.py:85-89`), and both writers save with `update_fields=["output", "updated_at"]` (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2154`, `products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:292`). Repeat firing on an unchanged target is deliberate (`receivers.py:77-79`), and the queued task is built for it: "The receiver re-fires on every TaskRun output save carrying the PR URL, so dedupe keys on the PR's CURRENT head" (`tasks.py:1125-1128`), with the head-keyed dedupe at `tasks.py:1202-1221`.
**Found:** the claim that webhooks cannot start this review holds only for `opened` and `ready_for_review`. `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS = frozenset({"synchronize", "reopened"})` (`tasks.py:49`) is what admits a delivery into the inbox carve-out (`tasks.py:167`), so any later push or reopen on the PR does start a review through the webhook leg.
**Found:** permanent loss therefore needs a conjunction: the broker is down in the dispatch window, and the run never receives another `output` save, and the PR never receives another push, and it is never reopened.
**Found:** the swallow is a deliberate, documented, tested contract, not an oversight. The function's docstring states it — "Fire-and-forget the hosted Stamphog review; the broker being down must never surface into the saver" (`receivers.py:213`) — the pre-existing ReviewHog leg is identical (`receivers.py:272-273`), and `test_stamphog_queue_failure_never_raises_into_the_save_path` (`products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:358-369`) pins it: "Same contract as the ReviewHog leg: the Celery broker being down must cost a log line, not break the run's output save".
**Impact:** does not meet the bar. The failure mode is fail-closed and observable: the outcome is one PR without a Stamphog verdict, logged at `logger.exception` (`receivers.py:233-234`). No approval lands on unreviewed code, no state is corrupted, no write is lost, and the result equals the pre-feature state. The remedy asked for — a persisted dispatch record, a post-commit publish, and a scheduled sweeper keyed on run plus PR URL — is new durability infrastructure that would upgrade the whole inbox trigger from best-effort to guaranteed delivery. That is a design decision for an alpha, flag-gated, default-off feature, and it applies equally to the pre-existing ReviewHog leg rather than to anything this change introduced. Under the overengineering and speculative-conjunction exclusions, it is not worth surfacing as a should-fix.
